question.text: Which of the following intermediaries is SEBI empowered to register and regulate under Section 11(2)?

answer.text: Stock brokers, share transfer agents and merchant bankers; portfolio managers, investment advisers and underwriters; and depositories, custodians and credit rating agencies
Only stock brokers, share transfer agents, and merchant bankers
Only portfolio managers, investment advisers, and underwriters
Only depositories, custodians, and credit rating agencies

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 11(2) empowers SEBI to register and regulate a comprehensive list of intermediaries including stock brokers, sub-brokers, share transfer agents, bankers to an issue, trustees of trust deeds, registrars, merchant bankers, underwriters, portfolio managers, investment advisers, depositories, custodians, CRAs, and others as notified. The Trap: Each of the three narrower groups lists genuine SEBI-regulated intermediaries, but none alone reflects the full scope of Section 11(2). The keyed option captures all three groups together. Note: Section 11(2) is deliberately broad and extensible — SEBI can also bring in further classes of intermediaries by notification, so the listed groups are illustrative, not exhaustive.
